newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: IBM rises on restructuring speculation.
newsitem.headline: IBM rises on restructuring speculation.

text.p: Computer and information technology firm IBM South Africa Group Ltd continued rising on Wednesday amid perceptions the firm's planned restructuring could enchance future earnings growth, dealers said.

"This is all about the restructuring which is going on at IBM. With the restructuring people see (IBM) a little bit healthier on their bottom line earnings in the future," one Johannesburg Stock Exchange (JSE) dealer said.
By about 1135 GMT the stock added 82 cents or 9.56 percent to 940 cents with 377,600 shares worth around 3.4 million rand changing hands.
"There could be positive news somewhere and guys are getting back into the stock at lower levels," another JSE dealer said.
But analysts said a lack of information from the company about the progress of the restructuring and what it entails made buying purely speculative.

"At the moment with the lack of information anybody buying the stock is really speculating. I can only imagine that some people are taking a punt as IBM are due to announce their results soon," said an analyst who asked not to be identified.
"Everybody takes a different view on what their earnings could be for the next year and that's really what's going to drive it," he added.
IBM was among leading percentage gainers on the JSE.
The share's recovery came after it took a tumble from a high of 10.90 rand on June 17. It started climbing from a low of 800 cents on July 7.
"I think its a good one to get into if you are into blue chips. It's been going on quite nicely for the past few days," a dealer said.

However, IBM said in April it expected to show a substantial trading loss for the six-month period ending June 30, 1997, due costs from its restructuring plan to focus on high growth areas in a bid to better its competition. The plan involves the retrenchment of about 550 staff.
IBM reports half-year results on August 19.
